Every evening around 100 food stalls are built on Fukuoka's pavements, each with about ten seats, and by 4 a.m. they're gone again. Here's how to get a seat, and which of the three areas to pick 👇

🍜 Nakasu, Tenjin or Nagahama: which one would you choose? Our pick is here 👉 https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-yatai-how-they-work

We checked every hour, rule and payment note against Fukuoka City's own pages and the stalls' listings.

🏮 THREE AREAS

1️⃣ Tenjin, our first-timer pick. The most variety, right by the trains. Kokinchan, famous for yaki-ramen (¥820), is about 2 minutes from Tenjin Station.

2️⃣ Nakasu, the classic scene. About 20 stalls in a row by the Naka River. Busiest 19:00 to 22:00, and the picture everyone has in mind.

3️⃣ Nagahama, the ramen row. The old home of Nagahama ramen, down to two stalls by 2021 and revived with seven new ones in June 2023. Smaller and quieter.

💴 HOW IT WORKS

Most stalls open between 18:30 and 19:00 and close around midnight. Most are cash only, and the city's guide says only about 10% take cards. Order at least one drink and one dish each, then move on to the next stall.

Our take: Tenjin for the first night, Nakasu for the photo, Nagahama for the last bowl of ramen.
